dedupe_keys.name: momentum agent based pedestrian simulation framework tu munich

description: MomenTUM is a Java agent-based pedestrian simulation framework developed at TU Munich's Chair of Computational Modeling and Simulation under Peter M. Kielar, currently at version 2.0.2. It is a generic, modular framework that integrates many pedestrian, utility and layout models and runs any number of behaviour models in combination, for example a cellular automaton linked to graph-based routing and an origin-destination matrix. A standalone JavaFX tool visualises XML layouts and CSV outputs, a Unity 3D visualiser is available on request, and published research configurations are shared in a users folder without a guarantee that they still run. Coverage: generic. Access: free source; the simulator and visualiser package as runnable jars. Licence: free for non-commercial research and education if the authors and papers are cited. Caveats: the documentation is incomplete, it targets JDK 1.8, and commercial use is not covered. Simulation uses: comparing pedestrian behaviour models for stations, venues and public spaces. Related records: Vadere and the Jülich pedestrian dynamics archive.
